applicability_reason: USFS response for a home used directly: one-storey wood-frame house with vinyl siding, asphalt shingles and a vented attic without ember-resistant vents, matching the DINS house group (wood/vinyl siding, asphalt roof); no mitigation or defensible-space credit.
demand_variable: conditional_flame_length_class_state: exact FSim conditional flame-length class state 0-6 (0 = no event; 1 < 2 ft ... 6 12+ ft) from USFS RDS-2016-0034-3 at the building location, with source_wildfire_product_id USFS_RDS_2016_0034_3_270M; burn probability is frequency (Hazard) and never a damage input
valid_domain_and_behavior: integers 0-6 evaluate by exact lookup; state 0 returns 0; fractional, non-numeric or out-of-range states are errors (INVALID_CLASS_STATE); no interpolation, no clamp
output_semantics: failure_unit_damage_ratio: expected repair cost as a fraction of structure value given a fire at the building location in that class (USFS relative structure loss, read as a repair-cost ratio)
uncertainty_meaning: none supplied (point value only); no sampleable spread; lifeform (tree / grass) and building-factor ranges in SENSITIVITY; outcomes are near all-or-nothing (DINS: 92% of damaged houses destroyed)
source_denominator: structure replacement cost new of the same building (the source loss scale runs from no damage to complete loss of the structure)
excluded_groups: contents;land;landscaping;site works;vehicles;smoke or ash contamination without fire damage;post-fire debris flow and erosion;business interruption
covered_fraction_status: not stated by the source: whole-structure loss with no component list; not set to 1.0 here
overlap_treatment: single assembly; embers, radiant heat, flame contact and building-to-building spread inside the one response (no add-on); all perils on one building in one event together at most 100% of structure value (consumer)
open_items: Shrub default (tree +5 points, grass -10 to -15 points). Flame-length class carries limited information about house loss (WFRE-C011).
